_comment: Every place AI-coding work happens on a machine, and what each one is.
CALLED `sources`, NOT `clis`. Half of these are not CLIs: copilot-chat and
kilocode are VS Code extensions, lmstudio is a desktop app, cowork is a Mac
app, cursor is an editor. `source` is also the word starreckon's own code
already uses — discoverSources(), src.source === "codex" — so the file is
named after the thing rather than after the half of it that came first.
`tools.json` was rejected: `tool` already means something else in both
programs (toolCallRounds, tool names in the digest), and a name that
collides with a concept you already count inside sessions is a name that
will be misread.
WHAT `kind` IS FOR. It is not a label. It decides WHERE discovery looks:
cli        a dotdir in $HOME                    ~/.codex, ~/.grok
extension  under a host editor's storage        {vscode}/User/globalStorage
app        the OS application-support tree      Library/Application Support
editor     its own workspace storage            varies
derived    not a tool at all — a counter that outlived its transcripts
That distinction is currently buried inside each reader, which is why
adding a source means editing code in two languages instead of a file.
`counted_by` IS THE HONEST FIELD. It says which programs can actually
produce a number for this source today. A name listed here that neither
program can read must report `no_reader` BY NAME on every run — never 0.
Zero is what a store that exists and is empty reports, and this system has
shipped that confusion seven times in four disguises.
`billed` distinguishes work that went through a provider account from work
that ran on this machine. It is a fact about WHERE THE COMPUTATION
HAPPENED, not a claim about money — nothing in either program attaches a
price to a token, and tests/no-cost.test.mjs enforces that.
DECLARE WHERE AND WHAT. CODE HOW. (author ruling, 2026-08-16)
Nothing that decides WHERE a source lives or WHAT fields it carries is
to be hardcoded in a reader. It is declared here — `kind` says where to
look, the entry says what to read — so adding a source is an edit to this
file and not to two programs in two languages.
What stays in code is HOW a number is computed: the dedup rule, the
Codex fork-lineage handling, the fact that bob's `input` already includes
its cache. That is behaviour, and the last spec design that tried to
carry behaviour was rejected for exactly that — a JSON glob is read
differently by Python's glob and Node's fs, and a rule in prose is a rule
nobody executes. Behaviour lives in code, held to the shared fixture.

states.absent: the store is not on this machine; nothing was found because there is nothing to find
states.empty: the store is present and holds no countable session
states.counted: the store is present and yielded sessions
states.unreadable: the store is present and could not be read — a locked directory, a corrupt database, a runtime missing a builtin
states.no_reader: declared here and this program has no reader bound to it; printed as a named gap, never as 0

sources.name: claude
sources.label: Claude Code
sources.note: the only CLI that writes its account email to disk, and the only one that deletes transcripts on a timer

sources.name: claude-orphans
sources.label: Claude Code — recovered counters
sources.note: NOT a tool. Recovers per-project lastTotal* counters in .claude.json for sessions whose transcripts were deleted, minus everything the claude reader already emitted. 4,172,332,033 tokens across 78 sessions on hp-laptop-linux. Ordering is load-bearing.

stores.label: claude-config-backups
stores.note: the profile's own timestamped copies. Declared because the DEFAULT profile keeps its config at ~/.claude.json, OUTSIDE ~/.claude — so no found config file has ~/.claude as its parent and its backups/ would never be reached by walking upward from a file.

sources.name: codex
sources.label: OpenAI Codex CLI
sources.note: total_token_usage is cumulative over the session LINEAGE, not the file. A fork inherits its parent's total; counting it whole double-counts the prefix once per fork.

sources.name: bob
sources.label: Bob
sources.note: SQLite, not JSONL. node:sqlite is a Node builtin so this costs no dependency, but it arrived in 22.5 — on an older runtime the store is present and UNREADABLE, which is not zero usage.

sources.name: clawspring
sources.label: Clawspring
sources.note: the format has no cache counters at all; those buckets are absent, not zero. A rollup recording 0 and 0 is not a session and is not emitted.

sources.name: copilot-chat
sources.label: GitHub Copilot Chat
sources.note: sums exactly one field — toolCallRounds[].thinking.tokens — into output. There is no input or prompt counter anywhere in the store, so the figure is a LOWER BOUND ON WHAT IS COUNTABLE and should be shown as one.

sources.name: kilocode
sources.label: Kilo Code
sources.note: spelled `kilocode` everywhere. The registry key was `kilo` on the starreckon side, so scanProvider('kilocode') threw and an api key under that name could never reach its reader.

sources.name: lmstudio
sources.label: LM Studio
sources.note: local models: the work ran on this machine and never went through a provider account. Counters live at the exact path messages[].versions[].steps[].genInfo.stats — searching the document for any genInfo is more permissive than deadreckon and diverges on the first malformed file.

sources.name: cowork
sources.label: Claude Cowork (macOS)
sources.note: an ordinary Mac app storing ordinary Claude Code profiles seven levels down, so the Claude parser reads them unchanged. deadreckon has no reader — it must report no_reader, not 0. The store is macOS-only and nobody has read the number in either direction yet.

stores.note: an ordinary Mac app store holding ordinary Claude Code profiles seven levels down: <account>/<org>/local_<uuid>/.claude/projects

sources.name: history
sources.label: Claude Code — session ledger
sources.note: CARRIES NO TOKEN COUNTS AT ALL. It proves a session existed, when, and in which project, and reaches months further back than the transcripts do. Giving it token fields would describe a file that does not have them.

sources.name: cursor
sources.label: Cursor
sources.note: NEITHER PROGRAM CAN COUNT IT. Listed so it reports no_reader by name on every run instead of being silently absent — a tool nobody has written a reader for and a tool nobody uses must not look the same.

_comment: Where a `stores[].base` starts, per platform. Home-relative segments
are joined under one of these. Values are SEGMENT LISTS, never joined
strings, so no separator convention has to be agreed between a Python
reader and a JavaScript one.
`{APPDATA}` is the only substitution: %APPDATA% on Windows, falling back
to AppData/Roaming under home when the variable is unset.
The two shapes that are not a literal path. Declared as RULES with
names, not as glob strings: a glob is read differently by Python's glob
and Node's fs, and declaring one here would move the drift rather than
remove it. The spec says where to start; the reader still walks.
store_rules.dotdir_contains: under the base, every DIRECTORY whose name starts with '.' and whose remainder contains this word — the rule that finds ~/.claude, ~/.claude-alt and ~/.my-claude alike
store_rules.channel: for base 'vscode': the editor directory under the base ('Code', 'Code - Insiders', 'VSCodium', 'Code - OSS')
